formulas.name: Second-order Taylor model
formulas.eq: f(x + p) ≈ f(x) + ∇f(x)ᵀp + ½ pᵀ∇²f(x) p
formulas.where: ∇f gradient, ∇²f Hessian (symmetric), p step from x
formulas.use: Local quadratic model behind every optimality condition and every Newton-type step.

formulas.name: First-order necessary condition
formulas.where: x* local minimizer of a smooth f in the interior (unconstrained)
formulas.use: Every smooth unconstrained local minimizer is a stationary point; solve ∇f = 0 to find the candidates.

formulas.name: Second-order conditions
formulas.where: ⪰ 0 positive semidefinite, ≻ 0 positive definite, evaluated at the stationary point x*
formulas.use: A stationary point with a positive definite Hessian is a strict local minimizer.

formulas.name: Quadratic gradient and minimizer
formulas.eq: f = ½xᵀHx + bᵀx + c:  ∇f = Hx + b,  ∇²f = H,  x* = −H⁻¹b
formulas.where: H symmetric n×n matrix, b vector, c scalar; x* is the unique minimizer when H ≻ 0
formulas.use: Model problem for line search, CG and Newton: the gradient is the residual Ax − b.

formulas.name: Eigenvalue classification
formulas.eq: Hv = λv:  all λᵢ > 0 min,  all λᵢ < 0 max,  mixed signs saddle
formulas.where: H Hessian at the stationary point, λᵢ its eigenvalues, v eigenvectors (principal curvature directions)
formulas.use: Classifies a critical point from the curvature along each Hessian eigenvector.

formulas.name: Two-variable test
formulas.eq: D = f_xx f_yy − f_xy²:  D > 0, f_xx > 0 min;  D > 0, f_xx < 0 max;  D < 0 saddle
formulas.where: Second partial derivatives evaluated at a point where f_x = f_y = 0; D = det H
formulas.use: Fast board check for 2D critical points; D = 0 calls for higher-order terms.

formulas.name: Descent step
formulas.where: α_k > 0 step length, p_k search direction, ∇f_k gradient at x_k
formulas.use: A direction with negative directional derivative guarantees f decreases for small enough α.

formulas.name: Sufficient decrease (Armijo)
formulas.where: 0 < c₁ < 1, typically c₁ = 10⁻⁴
formulas.use: Requires the actual decrease to be a fraction of the linear prediction, which rules out overly long steps.

formulas.name: Curvature condition
formulas.where: c₁ < c₂ < 1; typically c₂ = 0.9 for Newton and quasi-Newton, 0.1 for nonlinear CG
formulas.use: Requires the slope to have flattened enough, which rules out overly short steps and gives yᵀs > 0.

formulas.name: Strong Wolfe condition
formulas.where: Same c₁ < c₂ < 1 as the weak Wolfe conditions
formulas.use: Keeps the accepted point near a stationary point of the 1D function φ(α) = f(x_k + αp_k).

formulas.name: Exact step on a quadratic
formulas.where: f = ½xᵀAx − bᵀx with A ≻ 0, ∇f_k = Ax_k − b
formulas.use: Closed-form minimizer of f along p_k; for steepest descent it becomes gᵀg/(gᵀAg).

formulas.name: Steepest descent rate
formulas.where: Exact line search on a convex quadratic, κ = λ_max/λ_min of A, ‖e‖_A² = eᵀAe
formulas.use: Linear convergence that slows sharply as conditioning worsens, the zigzag picture on elongated contours.

formulas.name: Newton step
formulas.where: ∇²f_k Hessian, ∇f_k gradient at x_k; p_k minimizes the local quadratic model when ∇²f_k ≻ 0
formulas.use: Uses exact curvature and converges quadratically near a minimizer with a positive definite Hessian.

formulas.name: Quadratic convergence
formulas.where: C constant tied to the Hessian Lipschitz constant and ‖∇²f(x*)⁻¹‖, valid near x*
formulas.use: The number of correct digits roughly doubles per Newton iteration close to the solution.

formulas.name: Secant condition
formulas.where: s_k = x_{k+1} − x_k, y_k = ∇f_{k+1} − ∇f_k, B_{k+1} Hessian approximation
formulas.use: Makes the quasi-Newton model reproduce the observed gradient change along the last step.

formulas.name: BFGS update
formulas.eq: B₊ = B − (B s sᵀB)/(sᵀB s) + (y yᵀ)/(yᵀs)
formulas.where: s and y as in the secant condition; B₊ stays symmetric positive definite when yᵀs > 0
formulas.use: Rank-two update giving superlinear convergence from gradients alone.

formulas.name: Inverse BFGS update
formulas.eq: H₊ = (I − ρ s yᵀ) H (I − ρ y sᵀ) + ρ s sᵀ,  ρ = 1/(yᵀs)
formulas.where: H ≈ ∇²f⁻¹, so the step is p = −H∇f at O(n²) cost with no linear solve
formulas.use: Form used in practice and in the L-BFGS two-loop recursion.

formulas.name: Linear CG iteration
formulas.eq: α = rᵀr/(pᵀAp),  x₊ = x + αp,  r₊ = r + αAp,  β = r₊ᵀr₊/(rᵀr),  p₊ = −r₊ + βp
formulas.where: r = Ax − b residual (gradient), A ≻ 0 symmetric, p₀ = −r₀; directions satisfy p_iᵀAp_j = 0 for i ≠ j
formulas.use: Reaches the exact minimizer in at most n steps, with error bound driven by (√κ − 1)/(√κ + 1).

formulas.name: Trust-region subproblem
formulas.eq: min_p m_k(p) = f_k + g_kᵀp + ½ pᵀB_k p   s.t. ‖p‖ ≤ Δ_k
formulas.where: g_k gradient, B_k Hessian or approximation (indefinite allowed), Δ_k trust radius
formulas.use: Chooses step length and direction together by trusting the quadratic model only inside a ball.

formulas.name: Agreement ratio
formulas.where: Numerator actual reduction, denominator predicted reduction from the model
formulas.use: Measures how well the model predicted the step and drives acceptance and radius updates.

formulas.name: Radius update rule
formulas.eq: ρ < ¼: Δ ← ¼Δ;  ρ > ¾ and ‖p‖ = Δ: Δ ← min(2Δ, Δ_max);  accept p if ρ > η
formulas.where: η ∈ [0, ¼), typical Nocedal and Wright constants
formulas.use: Shrinks the region after poor predictions and expands it after good boundary steps.

formulas.name: Exact solution conditions
formulas.where: λ scalar multiplier on the trust-region constraint, ‖p*‖ ≤ Δ
formulas.use: Characterizes the global subproblem solution; λ acts like a Levenberg-Marquardt shift.

formulas.name: Cauchy point
formulas.eq: p_C = −τ (Δ/‖g‖) g,  τ = 1 if gᵀBg ≤ 0, else min(‖g‖³/(Δ gᵀBg), 1)
formulas.where: Minimizer of the model along −g inside the trust region
formulas.use: Cheap step whose decrease m(0) − m(p_C) ≥ ½‖g‖ min(Δ, ‖g‖/‖B‖) secures global convergence.

formulas.name: Dogleg path
formulas.eq: p(τ) = τ p_U for 0 ≤ τ ≤ 1;  p_U + (τ − 1)(p_B − p_U) for 1 ≤ τ ≤ 2
formulas.where: p_U = −(gᵀg/gᵀBg) g steepest descent minimizer, p_B = −B⁻¹g full Newton step, B ≻ 0
formulas.use: Approximates the subproblem by moving along a two-segment path and stopping at the boundary.

formulas.name: Lagrangian
formulas.eq: L(x, λ, μ) = f(x) + λᵀh(x) + μᵀg(x)
formulas.where: Problem: min f s.t. h(x) = 0, g(x) ≤ 0; λ equality multipliers, μ inequality multipliers
formulas.use: Folds the constraints into one function whose stationarity gives the KKT conditions.

formulas.name: KKT stationarity
formulas.where: Sign convention g ≤ 0 with L = f + λᵀh + μᵀg; requires a constraint qualification such as LICQ
formulas.use: At the optimum −∇f is a combination of the active constraint gradients.

formulas.name: Feasibility, dual sign, complementarity
formulas.where: Convention g ≤ 0 and minimization; λ free in sign
formulas.use: Each inactive constraint carries μᵢ = 0, and each active one pushes back with μᵢ ≥ 0.

formulas.name: Multiplier sensitivity
formulas.eq: df*/dc = −μ   for the constraint g(x) ≤ c
formulas.where: Convention L = f + μ(g − c), g ≤ c, minimization; f* optimal objective
formulas.use: The multiplier is the shadow price: relaxing c by Δc lowers f* by about μΔc.

formulas.name: Second-order sufficient condition
formulas.eq: dᵀ∇²ₓₓL(x*, λ*, μ*) d > 0  for all d ≠ 0 with ∇hᵀd = 0, ∇g_Aᵀd = 0
formulas.where: g_A active inequality constraints, assuming strict complementarity (μᵢ > 0 on each); d lies in the null space of the active constraint Jacobian
formulas.use: Curvature of the Lagrangian along the constraint surface confirms a strict local minimizer.

formulas.name: Equality QP KKT system
formulas.where: min ½xᵀQx + cᵀx s.t. Ax = b, with L = f + λᵀ(Ax − b)
formulas.use: One symmetric indefinite linear solve gives both the optimal point and its multipliers.

formulas.name: Quadratic penalty
formulas.eq: φ(x; μ) = f(x) + (μ/2) Σ hⱼ(x)² + (μ/2) Σ max(0, gᵢ(x))²
formulas.where: μ > 0 penalty parameter driven to ∞; convention g ≤ 0
formulas.use: Approaches x* from the infeasible side as μ grows, with Hessian conditioning growing like μ.

formulas.name: Log barrier
formulas.eq: φ(x; μ) = f(x) − μ Σ ln(−gᵢ(x)),  μ → 0⁺
formulas.where: Convention g ≤ 0; defined on the strict interior g < 0; multiplier estimate μᵢ ≈ −μ/gᵢ
formulas.use: Follows the central path of interior minimizers x*(μ) to the constrained optimum.

formulas.name: Augmented Lagrangian
formulas.eq: L_A = f + λᵀh + (μ/2)‖h‖²,   λ_{k+1} = λ_k + μ h(x_k)
formulas.where: Equality constraints h = 0, sign convention L = f + λᵀh
formulas.use: The multiplier update lets a moderate, finite μ reach x*, avoiding penalty ill-conditioning.

formulas.name: Exact ℓ1 penalty
formulas.eq: φ₁(x; ρ) = f(x) + ρ (Σ|hⱼ(x)| + Σ max(0, gᵢ(x))),   exact for ρ > ‖λ*‖∞
formulas.where: ‖λ*‖∞ largest multiplier magnitude at x*; φ₁ is nonsmooth at the constraint boundary
formulas.use: Recovers x* with one finite ρ and serves as the merit function in SQP line searches.

formulas.name: SQP subproblem
formulas.eq: min_p ∇fᵀp + ½pᵀ∇²ₓₓL p  s.t.  h + ∇hᵀp = 0,  g + ∇gᵀp ≤ 0
formulas.where: All quantities evaluated at x_k; ∇²ₓₓL exact or BFGS approximation of the Lagrangian Hessian
formulas.use: Each iteration solves a QP built from a quadratic model of L and linearized constraints.

formulas.name: SQP Newton-KKT system
formulas.where: A = ∂h/∂x Jacobian, convention L = f + λᵀh, equality-constrained case
formulas.use: SQP equals Newton's method on the KKT equations, so it converges quadratically near x*.

formulas.name: Quadratic response surface
formulas.eq: ŷ = β₀ + Σ βᵢxᵢ + Σ_{i≤j} βᵢⱼ xᵢxⱼ
formulas.where: k design variables, (k + 1)(k + 2)/2 coefficients, so at least that many samples
formulas.use: Workhorse polynomial surrogate, linear in its coefficients and fit by least squares.

formulas.name: Least squares normal equations
formulas.where: Φ_ij = φⱼ(xᵢ) basis matrix (n samples × m terms), w coefficients, y sampled responses
formulas.use: Minimizes ‖Φw − y‖²; solve with QR or SVD on Φ for numerical stability.

formulas.name: Ridge regularization
formulas.where: λ > 0 regularization weight on ‖w‖²
formulas.use: Shrinks the coefficients and stabilizes an ill-conditioned or underdetermined fit.

formulas.name: Radial basis function interpolant
formulas.eq: ŷ(x) = Σ wᵢ ψ(‖x − xᵢ‖),  Ψw = y,  Gaussian ψ(r) = exp(−(εr)²)
formulas.where: Ψ_ij = ψ(‖xᵢ − xⱼ‖), ε shape parameter, xᵢ sample sites
formulas.use: Interpolates scattered samples exactly in any dimension with one linear solve.

formulas.name: Coefficient of determination
formulas.eq: R² = 1 − SS_res/SS_tot,  SS_res = Σ(yᵢ − ŷᵢ)²,  SS_tot = Σ(yᵢ − ȳ)²
formulas.where: ȳ sample mean; adjusted R² = 1 − (1 − R²)(n − 1)/(n − p − 1) with p regressors
formulas.use: Fraction of response variance the fit explains; judge predictive accuracy by cross-validation.

formulas.name: Expected improvement
formulas.eq: EI = (f_min − ŷ) Φ(z) + s φ(z),   z = (f_min − ŷ)/s
formulas.where: ŷ and s kriging mean and standard deviation at x, Φ and φ standard normal CDF and PDF
formulas.use: Infill criterion balancing exploitation (low ŷ) and exploration (high s) in Bayesian optimization.

formulas.name: Convex function definition
formulas.where: x, y in a convex domain
formulas.use: Chord lies on or above the graph; for a convex problem every local minimizer is global.

formulas.name: First-order convexity
formulas.eq: f(y) ≥ f(x) + ∇f(x)ᵀ(y − x)  for all x, y
formulas.where: Differentiable f on a convex set
formulas.use: Every tangent plane is a global underestimator, so ∇f(x*) = 0 certifies a global minimizer.

formulas.name: Second-order convexity
formulas.where: Twice differentiable f on an open convex set; ⪰ 0 positive semidefinite
formulas.use: Quick convexity test: check the Hessian eigenvalues or leading minors.

formulas.name: Finite differences
formulas.eq: Forward: (f(x + heᵢ) − f(x))/h + O(h).  Central: (f(x + heᵢ) − f(x − heᵢ))/(2h) + O(h²)
formulas.where: eᵢ unit vector, h step; forward optimum h ≈ √ε_f, central optimum h ≈ ε_f^(1/3), ε_f function precision
formulas.use: Simplest gradient route, with step size balancing truncation error against subtractive cancellation.

formulas.name: Complex step
formulas.where: i = √−1, h tiny (10⁻²⁰ to 10⁻³⁰), f implemented in complex arithmetic
formulas.use: Free of subtractive cancellation, so it delivers derivatives to machine precision.

formulas.name: Adjoint method
formulas.where: R(x, u) = 0 governing residuals, u state, ψ adjoint vector (Martins and Ning convention)
formulas.use: One linear solve per output gives the full gradient, ideal for many design variables and few functions.

formulas.name: Pareto dominance
formulas.eq: x₁ ≺ x₂ ⟺ fᵢ(x₁) ≤ fᵢ(x₂) for all i, and fⱼ(x₁) < fⱼ(x₂) for some j
formulas.where: Minimization of objectives f₁ … f_m; the Pareto set is the nondominated designs
formulas.use: Defines the trade-off front from which the decision maker picks a design.

formulas.name: Weighted sum
formulas.eq: min Σ wᵢ f̄ᵢ(x),   wᵢ ≥ 0,  Σ wᵢ = 1,   f̄ᵢ = (fᵢ − fᵢ^utopia)/(fᵢ^nadir − fᵢ^utopia)
formulas.where: f̄ᵢ normalized objectives, utopia from individual minima, nadir from worst Pareto values
formulas.use: Sweeping the weights traces the convex portions of the Pareto front.

formulas.name: ε-constraint method
formulas.eq: min f₁(x)  s.t.  fᵢ(x) ≤ εᵢ,  i = 2 … m
formulas.where: εᵢ bounds swept across the range of each secondary objective
formulas.use: Traces the whole Pareto front, including nonconvex portions.

formulas.name: Particle swarm update
formulas.eq: v₊ = w v + c₁r₁(p_best − x) + c₂r₂(g_best − x),   x₊ = x + v₊
formulas.where: w inertia, c₁ cognitive and c₂ social coefficients, r₁, r₂ uniform on [0, 1]
formulas.use: Each particle blends momentum, its own best point and the swarm best to explore globally.

formulas.name: Simulated annealing acceptance
formulas.eq: P(accept) = 1 if Δf ≤ 0,  exp(−Δf/T) if Δf > 0
formulas.where: Δf = f_new − f_current, T temperature reduced by a cooling schedule such as T_{k+1} = 0.9T_k
formulas.use: Accepting some uphill moves at high T lets the search escape local minima.

formulas.name: Nelder-Mead reflection
formulas.eq: x_r = x_c + α(x_c − x_w),  α = 1;  expansion α = 2, contraction α = ±½
formulas.where: x_w worst vertex, x_c centroid of the other n vertices of the n + 1 point simplex
formulas.use: Moves the simplex away from its worst point using function values only.

formulas.name: MDF architecture
formulas.eq: min f(x, y(x))  s.t.  g(x, y(x)) ≤ 0,  y from a full MDA at every x
formulas.where: y coupling variables solved by Gauss-Seidel, Jacobi or Newton iteration
formulas.use: Every optimizer iterate is multidisciplinary feasible, with the fewest optimization variables.

formulas.name: IDF architecture
formulas.eq: min f(x, yᵗ)  s.t.  g ≤ 0,  yᵗᵢ − Yᵢ(x, yᵗ_{j≠i}) = 0
formulas.where: yᵗ coupling targets added as design variables, Yᵢ discipline i output
formulas.use: Decouples the disciplines so they run in parallel, with consistency reached at the optimum.

formulas.name: Coupled Newton solve
formulas.where: Rᵢ discipline residuals, uᵢ discipline states; off-diagonal blocks are the coupling
formulas.use: Converges the MDA quadratically, and the same Jacobian gives coupled derivatives.

formulas.name: Factorial run counts
formulas.eq: Full factorial N = Lᵏ;  two-level fractional N = 2^(k − p)
formulas.where: L levels, k factors, p generators; resolution sets which effects alias
formulas.use: Sizes a screening or response-surface experiment before any runs are made.

formulas.name: Central composite design
formulas.eq: N = 2ᵏ + 2k + n_c,  axial distance α = (2ᵏ)^(1/4) for rotatability
formulas.where: 2ᵏ factorial corners, 2k axial (star) points, n_c center points
formulas.use: Supplies enough points to fit a full quadratic response surface.

formulas.name: Main effect
formulas.where: ȳ(A±) mean response over runs with factor A at its high or low level
formulas.use: Average change in response when one factor moves from low to high.

formulas.name: Master equation
formulas.where: α thrust lapse T/T_SL, β = W/W_TO, q dynamic pressure, n load factor, C_DR extra drag, P_s = d/dt(h + V²/2g)
formulas.use: Mattingly energy balance turning every mission requirement into a T/W versus W/S constraint curve.

formulas.name: Simplified master equation
formulas.where: K₂ = 0 and C_DR = 0 in the full form; K₁ = 1/(πeAR)
formulas.use: Parasite term falls with W/S, induced term grows with W/S, and the climb and acceleration terms add on top.

formulas.name: Stall and landing constraint
formulas.where: β weight fraction at the condition, ρ density, C_Lmax for the relevant flap setting
formulas.use: A vertical line on the constraint diagram, with the feasible region to its left.

formulas.name: Takeoff constraint
formulas.where: k_TO = V_TO/V_stall (about 1.2), s_TO ground roll length, simple form with drag and friction neglected
formulas.use: Straight line through the origin whose slope falls with longer field length, higher ρ and higher C_Lmax.

formulas.name: Constant-speed bucket
formulas.where: From the simplified master equation at constant altitude and speed
formulas.use: The minimum T/W of a cruise or turn constraint sits where parasite and induced terms are equal (max L/D).

formulas.name: Breguet range (jet)
formulas.where: c_t thrust-specific fuel consumption (1/s, fuel weight flow per thrust), constant V, L/D, c_t
formulas.use: Range grows with V(L/D)/c_t, maximized at √C_L/C_D max where C_D0 = 3KC_L².

formulas.name: Breguet range (propeller)
formulas.where: η_p propeller efficiency, c_p power-specific fuel consumption in weight per energy (1/length)
formulas.use: Prop range is maximized at (L/D)_max, where C_D0 = KC_L².

formulas.name: Jet endurance
formulas.where: c_t thrust-specific fuel consumption (1/s), constant L/D and c_t
formulas.use: Jet endurance depends on L/D alone, so it peaks at (L/D)_max.

formulas.name: Maximum lift-to-drag
formulas.where: Parabolic polar C_D = C_D0 + KC_L², K = 1/(πeAR)
formulas.use: At C_L* induced drag equals parasite drag, the minimum drag condition.

formulas.name: Rate of climb
formulas.eq: R/C = V sin γ = (P_A − P_R)/W = (T − D)V/W
formulas.where: P_A = TV power available, P_R = DV power required, steady climb
formulas.use: Excess power per weight sets climb rate; ceilings occur where its maximum reaches 100 ft/min (service) and 0 (absolute).

formulas.name: Takeoff ground roll
formulas.eq: s_LO ≈ 1.44 W²/(g ρ S C_Lmax T)
formulas.where: V_LO = 1.2V_stall, T average thrust, drag and rolling friction neglected (Anderson)
formulas.use: Ground roll scales with W/S and inversely with ρ, C_Lmax and T/W.

formulas.name: Stall boundary
formulas.where: V_e equivalent airspeed, ρ₀ sea-level density; use C_L,neg for the negative side
formulas.use: Parabolic left edge of the maneuver envelope, the most load the wing can produce at each speed.

formulas.name: Equivalent airspeed
formulas.where: V true airspeed, σ = ρ/ρ₀ density ratio
formulas.use: Plotting in EAS gives one envelope for all altitudes, since q = ½ρ₀V_e².

formulas.name: Maneuvering (corner) speed
formulas.where: V_S1 1 g stall speed, n_max positive limit load factor
formulas.use: Where the stall curve meets the limit load line, the speed for maximum instantaneous turn rate.

formulas.name: Gust load factor
formulas.eq: Δn = ρ₀ U_de V_e a K_g/(2W/S),   K_g = 0.88μ_g/(5.3 + μ_g),  μ_g = 2(W/S)/(ρ c̄ a g)
formulas.where: U_de derived gust velocity (EAS), a lift slope per rad, K_g gust alleviation factor, c̄ mean chord
formulas.use: Gust lines radiate from n = 1 at zero speed with slope rising with a and falling with W/S.

formulas.name: FAR 25 limit load factors
formulas.where: W design takeoff weight in lb
formulas.use: Sets the horizontal limit lines of a transport category maneuver envelope.

formulas.name: Ultimate load
formulas.where: 1.5 factor of safety on limit load (FAR 23 and 25)
formulas.use: Structure carries limit load with no permanent deformation and ultimate load for at least 3 s.

formulas.name: Uninstalled thrust
formulas.eq: F = ṁ_e V_e − ṁ₀V₀ + (p_e − p₀)A_e  ≈  ṁ(V_e − V₀) + (p_e − p₀)A_e
formulas.where: ṁ₀ air mass flow, ṁ_e = ṁ₀ + ṁ_f exit flow, V₀ flight speed, p_e, A_e nozzle exit pressure and area
formulas.use: Momentum flux change plus pressure thrust; ṁ₀V₀ is the ram drag.

formulas.name: Propulsive efficiency
formulas.where: Single stream, ṁ_f ≪ ṁ, perfectly expanded nozzle
formulas.use: Large mass flow at small velocity increment gives high η_p, the case for high bypass ratio.

formulas.name: Ideal Brayton thermal efficiency
formulas.where: τ_r ram temperature ratio, π_c compressor pressure ratio, calorically perfect gas
formulas.use: Thermal efficiency rises with overall pressure ratio, including ram compression at high Mach.

formulas.name: Overall efficiency and TSFC
formulas.eq: η_o = η_th η_p = F V₀/(ṁ_f h_PR),   TSFC = ṁ_f/F
formulas.where: h_PR fuel heating value, ṁ_f fuel mass flow
formulas.use: Links cycle and propulsive efficiencies to fuel burn: TSFC = V₀/(η_o h_PR).

formulas.name: Component isentropic efficiency
formulas.where: s subscript isentropic end state at the same exit pressure, T_t3s/T_t2 = π_c^((γ−1)/γ)
formulas.use: Actual compressors need more work and actual turbines deliver less, shown as lines slanting right on T-s.

formulas.name: Stagnation relations
formulas.where: Isentropic, calorically perfect gas; T_t, p_t stagnation temperature and pressure
formulas.use: Converts static conditions to total conditions at each engine station.

formulas.name: Kutta-Joukowski theorem
formulas.where: L' lift per unit span, Γ = −∮V·ds with the line integral taken counterclockwise (Anderson), so clockwise circulation gives positive lift
formulas.use: Ties two-dimensional lift directly to circulation set by the Kutta condition.

formulas.name: Thin airfoil theory
formulas.eq: c_l = 2π(α − α_L0),   c_m,c/4 constant,  x_ac = c/4
formulas.where: α_L0 zero-lift angle (negative for positive camber), α in radians
formulas.use: Lift slope 2π per radian and aerodynamic center at the quarter chord for thin airfoils.

formulas.name: Induced drag
formulas.eq: C_Di = C_L²/(π e AR),   α_i = C_L/(πAR) for elliptic loading
formulas.where: e span efficiency (1 for elliptic lift distribution), AR = b²/S
formulas.use: Lifting line result: induced drag falls with aspect ratio and rises with C_L².

formulas.name: Finite wing lift slope
formulas.where: a₀ section lift slope per rad, e₁ span efficiency factor for lift slope
formulas.use: A finite wing has a lower lift slope than its airfoil because of downwash.

formulas.name: Prandtl-Glauert correction
formulas.where: C_p,0 incompressible pressure coefficient, subsonic linearized flow, M∞ < about 0.7
formulas.use: Compressibility amplifies pressure coefficients and lift slope by 1/√(1 − M²).

formulas.name: Sweep and normal Mach
formulas.where: Λ sweep angle of the isobars or quarter chord line (simple sweep theory)
formulas.use: Sweep lowers the Mach number the section feels, raising the drag-divergence Mach.

formulas.name: Momentum theory hover
formulas.eq: T = 2ρA v_i²,   v_i = √(T/(2ρA)),   far wake velocity w = 2v_i
formulas.where: A rotor disk area, v_i induced velocity at the disk, ρ density
formulas.use: Actuator disk result linking thrust to induced flow through the rotor.

formulas.name: Ideal hover power
formulas.where: T thrust, disk loading T/A
formulas.use: Lower disk loading means less power per thrust, and thin air demands a proportionally larger ρA.

formulas.name: Figure of merit
formulas.where: P actual shaft power in hover
formulas.use: Hover efficiency of a rotor; good rotors reach about 0.7 to 0.8.

formulas.name: Thrust coefficient
formulas.where: Ω rotor speed, R radius, σ solidity, a lift slope, θ₀ collective, λ inflow ratio; untwisted, uniform inflow
formulas.use: Blade element momentum link from collective pitch and tip speed to thrust.

formulas.name: Advance ratio and tip speeds
formulas.eq: μ = V/(ΩR),   advancing tip ΩR + V,  retreating tip ΩR − V
formulas.where: V forward speed; ψ = 90° advancing side, ψ = 270° retreating side
formulas.use: Advancing tip Mach and retreating blade stall bound helicopter forward speed.

formulas.name: Induced velocity in fast forward flight
formulas.where: Glauert high-speed approximation, V ≫ v_i
formulas.use: Induced power falls with forward speed, giving the power bucket at moderate speed.

formulas.name: Takeoff weight sizing
formulas.where: W_f/W₀ fuel fraction, W_e/W₀ empty weight fraction (a function of W₀)
formulas.use: Solved by iteration on W₀, the core of Raymer conceptual sizing.

formulas.name: Empty weight fraction
formulas.where: A, C statistical constants per aircraft class (C small and negative), K_vs = 1.04 variable sweep, else 1.00
formulas.use: Historical trend for structure and systems weight that closes the sizing loop.

formulas.name: Fuel fraction
formulas.where: Product of mission segment weight fractions; 6% for reserve and trapped fuel
formulas.use: Converts the mission profile into total fuel required.

formulas.name: Cruise and loiter fractions
formulas.eq: Cruise: Wᵢ/Wᵢ₋₁ = exp(−Rc/(V L/D));  loiter: Wᵢ/Wᵢ₋₁ = exp(−Ec/(L/D))
formulas.where: c TSFC (1/s), R range, E endurance, V speed; Breguet equations inverted
formulas.use: Mission segment weight fractions for the long segments; short ones use historical values.

formulas.name: Divergence dynamic pressure
formulas.where: Typical section: K_θ torsional stiffness, e distance from aerodynamic center aft to elastic axis, a lift slope
formulas.use: Torsional stiffness against aerodynamic twisting moment; moving the elastic axis forward raises q_D.

formulas.name: Control reversal dynamic pressure
formulas.where: Typical section: C_Lδ, C_Mδ lift and moment per flap angle (C_Mδ < 0 about the AC), c chord
formulas.use: At q_R the twist from the control surface cancels its lift increment; above q_R roll authority reverses.

formulas.name: Tangential equation
formulas.eq: m dV/dt = T cos(α + ε) − D − W sin γ
formulas.where: ε thrust angle relative to the zero-lift or body line, γ flight-path angle, point mass
formulas.use: Thrust component along the path accelerates the aircraft against drag and the weight component.

formulas.name: Normal equation
formulas.eq: mV dγ/dt = L + T sin(α + ε) − W cos γ
formulas.where: Wings-level flight in the vertical plane
formulas.use: Net normal force supplies the centripetal force that curves the flight path.

formulas.name: Path kinematics
formulas.eq: dh/dt = V sin γ,   dx/dt = V cos γ
formulas.where: h altitude, x horizontal distance, still air
formulas.use: Converts speed and flight-path angle into climb rate and ground distance.

formulas.name: Level coordinated turn
formulas.eq: n = 1/cos φ,   ω = g√(n² − 1)/V,   R = V²/(g√(n² − 1))
formulas.where: φ bank angle, ω turn rate, R turn radius, √(n² − 1) = tan φ
formulas.use: Lift tilted by the bank angle supplies the horizontal centripetal force.

formulas.name: Vertical pull-up
formulas.eq: n = 1 + V²/(gR)   at the bottom of the loop
formulas.where: R radius of curvature of the path in the vertical plane
formulas.use: Lift supports the weight plus the centripetal force mV²/R.

formulas.name: Energy height and excess power
formulas.eq: h_e = h + V²/(2g),   P_s = (T − D)V/W = dh/dt + (V/g)dV/dt
formulas.where: P_s specific excess power with units of velocity
formulas.use: Excess power can be spent on climb, acceleration, or a blend, the basis of energy maneuverability.

formulas.name: Parabolic drag polar
formulas.eq: C_D = C_D0 + K C_L²,   K = 1/(π e AR)
formulas.where: C_D0 zero-lift drag, e Oswald efficiency factor
formulas.use: Splits drag into parasite and lift-dependent parts for all performance estimates.

formulas.name: Component drag buildup
formulas.eq: C_D0 = Σ(C_f,c FF_c Q_c S_wet,c)/S_ref + C_D,misc + C_D,L&P
formulas.where: C_f skin friction, FF form factor, Q interference factor, L&P leakage and protuberance
formulas.use: Raymer method summing each component's friction drag corrected for shape and installation.

formulas.name: Skin friction coefficients
formulas.where: Re = ρVl/μ based on component length, flat plate averages
formulas.use: Flat-plate friction baseline for the buildup; turbulent flow gives much higher C_f.

formulas.name: Wing form factor
formulas.where: (x/c)_m chordwise position of maximum thickness, Λ_m sweep of the max-thickness line (Raymer)
formulas.use: Scales flat-plate friction up for thickness supervelocity and pressure drag.

formulas.name: Flap lift increment
formulas.where: ΔC_lmax airfoil increment from the device, S_flapped wing area spanned by the flap, Λ_HL hinge line sweep
formulas.use: Raymer estimate of wing C_Lmax gain from flaps and slats.

formulas.name: Stall speed
formulas.where: W weight, S wing area, C_Lmax for the configuration
formulas.use: High-lift devices raise C_Lmax to cut stall, approach and landing speeds.

formulas.name: Pitch stiffness and static margin
formulas.eq: C_mα = C_Lα(h − h_n) = −C_Lα·SM,   SM = h_n − h
formulas.where: h = x_cg/c̄, h_n = x_np/c̄ measured aft from the leading edge of the MAC
formulas.use: Static stability needs C_mα < 0; trim at positive lift then needs C_m0 > 0.

formulas.name: Stick-fixed neutral point
formulas.where: a_t tail lift slope, a wing-body lift slope, η tail efficiency, dε/dα downwash gradient
formulas.use: CG location for neutral stability; the tail moves it aft of the wing-body AC.

formulas.name: Tail volume coefficients
formulas.eq: V_H = l_t S_t/(c̄ S),   V_V = l_v S_v/(b S)
formulas.where: l_t, l_v tail moment arms (Raymer: wing quarter-chord MAC to tail quarter-chord MAC; stability texts use the CG), S_t, S_v tail areas, c̄ mean chord, b span
formulas.use: Primary sizing parameters for horizontal and vertical tails from historical values.

formulas.name: Trim elevator deflection
formulas.eq: δ_e,trim = −(C_m0 C_Lα + C_mα C_L,trim)/(C_Lα C_mδe − C_mα C_Lδe)
formulas.where: From C_L = C_Lα α + C_Lδe δ_e and C_m = C_m0 + C_mα α + C_mδe δ_e = 0
formulas.use: Elevator needed to fly at a given lift coefficient; forward CG demands the most.

formulas.name: Lateral-directional static stability
formulas.where: β sideslip angle (nose left of the wind positive), C_n yawing and C_l rolling moment
formulas.use: Vertical tail yaws the nose into the wind; dihedral, high wing and sweep roll the wings level.

formulas.name: Phugoid approximation
formulas.where: Lanchester approximation, damping ratio ζ ≈ 1/(√2 L/D)
formulas.use: Long-period exchange of speed and altitude at nearly constant α.

formulas.name: Deformation gradient
formulas.eq: F = ∂x/∂X = I + Grad u,   J = det F > 0,   dv = J dV
formulas.where: X reference position, x = χ(X, t) current position, u = x − X displacement
formulas.use: Maps reference line elements to current ones, dx = F dX; J is the local volume ratio.

formulas.name: Cauchy-Green tensors
formulas.eq: C = FᵀF,   B = FFᵀ,   λ_N² = N·CN
formulas.where: C right (referential), B left (spatial), λ_N stretch of a fiber along unit vector N
formulas.use: Rotation-free measures of deformation; their eigenvalues are the squared principal stretches.

formulas.name: Green-Lagrange strain
formulas.eq: E = ½(C − I) = ½(H + Hᵀ + HᵀH),   H = Grad u
formulas.where: Components E_IJ = ½(u_I,J + u_J,I + u_K,I u_K,J); ds² − dS² = 2dX·E dX
formulas.use: Exact strain for large deformations and rotations, zero for any rigid motion.

formulas.name: Small strain and rotation
formulas.where: Valid for small displacement gradients; ε_ij = ½(u_i,j + u_j,i), γ_12 = 2ε_12
formulas.use: Linearized strain used in classical elasticity; ω is the infinitesimal rigid rotation.

formulas.name: Polar decomposition
formulas.eq: F = RU = VR,   U = √C,   V = √B,   V = RURᵀ
formulas.where: R proper orthogonal rotation, U and V symmetric positive definite stretch tensors
formulas.use: Separates any deformation into a pure stretch and a rigid rotation.

formulas.name: 2D strain compatibility
formulas.where: Tensor shear strain ε₁₂ = γ₁₂/2, small strain, simply connected body
formulas.use: Guarantees the strain field integrates to a single-valued continuous displacement.

formulas.name: Cauchy's theorem
formulas.eq: t = σn,   tᵢ = σᵢⱼnⱼ,   σ_n = n·σn
formulas.where: t traction on a surface with outward unit normal n, σ Cauchy (true) stress
formulas.use: Stress tensor gives the traction on every plane through a point.

formulas.name: Equilibrium and symmetry
formulas.eq: div σ + b = 0 (σᵢⱼ,ⱼ + bᵢ = 0),   σ = σᵀ
formulas.where: b body force per current volume; symmetry from angular momentum with no body couples
formulas.use: Pointwise statics that every admissible stress field satisfies, with σn = t on traction boundaries.

formulas.name: Plane principal stresses
formulas.eq: σ₁,₂ = (σ_x + σ_y)/2 ± √(((σ_x − σ_y)/2)² + τ_xy²),   tan 2θ_p = 2τ_xy/(σ_x − σ_y)
formulas.where: Mohr circle center (σ_x + σ_y)/2, radius equal to the square root term
formulas.use: Gives principal stresses and maximum in-plane shear (the radius) for a 2D stress state.

formulas.name: Invariants and characteristic equation
formulas.eq: s³ − I₁s² + I₂s − I₃ = 0,  I₁ = tr σ,  I₂ = ½[(tr σ)² − tr(σ²)],  I₃ = det σ
formulas.where: Roots s are the principal stresses; I₂ = σ₁σ₂ + σ₂σ₃ + σ₃σ₁
formulas.use: Frame-independent scalars used in yield criteria and constitutive laws.

formulas.name: Von Mises stress
formulas.where: J₂ = ½ s:s second invariant of the deviatoric stress s = σ − (tr σ/3)I
formulas.use: Ductile yield occurs when σ_vm reaches the uniaxial yield stress σ_y.

formulas.name: Objectivity of Cauchy stress
formulas.eq: σ* = Q σ Qᵀ,   constitutive law: σ̂(QF) = Q σ̂(F) Qᵀ
formulas.where: Q any proper orthogonal tensor (rigid rotation of the observer or of the deformed body)
formulas.use: Frame indifference requirement that every admissible constitutive law satisfies.

formulas.name: Generalized Hooke's law
formulas.where: C fourth-order stiffness with minor and major symmetry: 21 constants anisotropic, 9 orthotropic, 2 isotropic
formulas.use: Linear elastic link between stress and small strain.

formulas.name: Isotropic stiffness form
formulas.where: λ, μ Lamé constants, μ = G shear modulus
formulas.use: Isotropic Hooke's law with two independent constants.

formulas.name: Isotropic compliance form
formulas.where: E Young's modulus, ν Poisson's ratio; ε₁₁ = [σ₁₁ − ν(σ₂₂ + σ₃₃)]/E
formulas.use: Engineering form for strains from a known stress state.

formulas.name: Elastic constant relations
formulas.where: K bulk modulus; positive definiteness requires −1 < ν < ½
formulas.use: Converts between any pair of isotropic constants; K grows without bound as ν → ½.

formulas.name: Plane stress stiffness
formulas.where: σ₃ⱼ = 0, γ₁₂ = 2ε₁₂ engineering shear strain
formulas.use: Constitutive matrix for thin plates and membranes loaded in plane.

formulas.name: Strain energy density
formulas.eq: W = ½ σ:ε = μ ε:ε + (λ/2)(tr ε)²,   σ = ∂W/∂ε
formulas.where: Linear isotropic elasticity, small strain
formulas.use: Stored elastic energy per volume, positive definite for a stable material.

formulas.name: Airy stress function
formulas.where: Plane stress or plane strain with zero body force
formulas.use: Satisfies equilibrium identically, leaving compatibility to solve.

formulas.name: Biharmonic equation
formulas.where: Compatibility in terms of φ for isotropic linear elasticity, zero body force
formulas.use: Governing equation of 2D elasticity; polynomial and Fourier φ give beam and strip solutions.

formulas.name: Airy function in polar coordinates
formulas.where: r, θ polar coordinates, zero body force
formulas.use: Natural form for holes, wedges, disks and curved bars.

formulas.name: Plane strain out-of-plane stress
formulas.where: Long body constrained along z, isotropic linear elastic
formulas.use: Out-of-plane stress that holds the long body at zero axial strain.

formulas.name: Plane stress to plane strain conversion
formulas.eq: Replace E with E/(1 − ν²) and ν with ν/(1 − ν)
formulas.where: Apply to a plane stress displacement or strain solution to obtain the plane strain one
formulas.use: One 2D solution serves both cases since the Airy stress field is the same.

formulas.name: Kirsch hole solution
formulas.eq: σ_θθ(a, θ) = σ₀(1 − 2 cos 2θ),   max 3σ₀ at θ = ±90°
formulas.where: Circular hole of radius a in an infinite plate under remote uniaxial σ₀ along θ = 0
formulas.use: Stress concentration factor K_t = 3, with −σ₀ at the hole edge on the load axis.

formulas.name: Thin-walled cylinder
formulas.where: p internal gauge pressure, r mean radius, t wall thickness, r/t > about 10, closed ends
formulas.use: Hoop stress is twice the axial stress, so longitudinal seams carry the critical load.

formulas.name: Thin-walled sphere
formulas.where: Same assumptions as the thin cylinder
formulas.use: A sphere carries pressure at half the cylinder hoop stress, the lightest pressure vessel.

formulas.name: Lamé solution (cylinder)
formulas.eq: σ_rr = A − B/r²,   σ_θθ = A + B/r²
formulas.where: A, B constants from the radial boundary conditions, axisymmetric, plane strain or plane stress
formulas.use: General thick-walled cylinder stress field; σ_rr + σ_θθ = 2A is uniform.

formulas.name: Thick cylinder, internal pressure
formulas.eq: σ_θθ = p a²(1 + b²/r²)/(b² − a²),  σ_rr = p a²(1 − b²/r²)/(b² − a²)
formulas.where: a inner, b outer radius, internal pressure p, zero external pressure
formulas.use: Peak hoop stress at the bore: σ_θθ(a) = p(b² + a²)/(b² − a²).

formulas.name: Closed-end axial stress
formulas.where: End caps carry the pressure resultant pπa² over the wall area π(b² − a²)
formulas.use: Uniform axial stress in a thick closed cylinder, equal to A in the Lamé solution.

formulas.name: Thick sphere
formulas.eq: σ_rr = A − B/r³,   σ_θθ = A + B/(2r³)
formulas.where: A, B from boundary pressures at the inner and outer radii, spherical symmetry
formulas.use: Thick spherical shell field; stresses decay as 1/r³ away from the inner surface.

formulas.name: Flexure formula
formulas.where: y distance from the neutral axis, positive toward the fiber the moment puts in tension; I about the neutral axis
formulas.use: Linear bending stress across the depth, largest at the extreme fiber, zero at the centroid.

formulas.name: Moment-curvature relation
formulas.where: w deflection positive upward, M positive for sagging (compression on top), small slopes
formulas.use: Integrate twice with boundary conditions to get the deflection curve.

formulas.name: Euler-Bernoulli beam equation
formulas.where: w deflection and q load both positive upward; the sign linking shear V to w‴ varies by text
formulas.use: Fourth-order equation needing two boundary conditions at each end.

formulas.name: Section properties
formulas.eq: Rectangle I = bh³/12,  circle I = πr⁴/4,  parallel axis I = I_c + A d²
formulas.where: b width, h depth, I_c about the centroid, d distance from the centroidal axis
formulas.use: Building blocks for built-up and thin-walled section inertias.

formulas.name: Principal axes
formulas.where: I_x = ∫y²dA, I_y = ∫x²dA, I_xy = ∫xy dA about centroidal axes; θ_p counterclockwise from x (Gere convention)
formulas.use: Along principal axes I_xy = 0 and bending in each plane decouples.

formulas.name: Standard deflections
formulas.eq: Cantilever tip: PL³/(3EI), wL⁴/(8EI).  Simply supported center: PL³/(48EI), 5wL⁴/(384EI)
formulas.where: P end or midspan point load, w uniform load per length
formulas.use: Superposition building blocks for indeterminate beams and quick checks.

formulas.name: Open-section shear flow
formulas.eq: q(s) = (V/I) Q(s),   Q(s) = ∫₀ˢ y t ds,   τ = q/t
formulas.where: s measured from a free edge where q = 0, y from the neutral axis, symmetric section, V through the shear center
formulas.use: Builds the shear flow distribution and locates the shear center by moment balance.

formulas.name: Bredt-Batho
formulas.eq: T = 2 A q,   τ = q/t = T/(2At)
formulas.where: A area enclosed by the wall median line, q constant shear flow in a single closed cell
formulas.use: Torque carried by a closed thin-walled tube under pure torsion.

formulas.name: Closed-cell twist and J
formulas.where: G shear modulus; the same θ′ in every cell of a multicell section
formulas.use: Compatibility equation that fixes redundant shear flows and gives closed-section stiffness.

formulas.name: Thin open-section torsion
formulas.eq: J = Σ b t³/3,   τ_max = G t_max θ′ = T t_max/J
formulas.where: b strip length, t strip thickness, St Venant torsion with free warping
formulas.use: Open sections have small J, so they are far more flexible in torsion than closed ones.

formulas.name: Circular shaft torsion
formulas.eq: τ = T r/J,   θ′ = T/(GJ),   J = πd⁴/32
formulas.where: J polar moment, d diameter; hollow J = π(d_o⁴ − d_i⁴)/32
formulas.use: Shear stress grows linearly with radius and peaks at the outer surface.

formulas.name: Prandtl stress function
formulas.where: ψ = 0 on the boundary of a solid section; membrane analogy: slope gives τ, volume gives T/2
formulas.use: Solves St Venant torsion for noncircular solid sections.

formulas.name: Strain energy of a slender member
formulas.where: M bending moment, N axial force, T torque, linear elastic
formulas.use: Energy expression for Castigliano and unit load methods; bending dominates slender members.

formulas.name: Castigliano's second theorem
formulas.where: U* complementary energy in terms of loads, δᵢ displacement at Pᵢ along its direction
formulas.use: Find a deflection by differentiating energy with respect to a real or dummy load.

formulas.name: Unit load method
formulas.eq: δ = ∫ M m/(EI) dx + ∫ N n/(EA) dx
formulas.where: M, N from real loads; m, n from a unit load at the point and direction of δ
formulas.use: Virtual work route to any single displacement or rotation.

formulas.name: Minimum total potential energy
formulas.eq: Π = U − W_ext,   δΠ = 0,   δ²Π > 0 for stable equilibrium
formulas.where: W_ext = Σ Pᵢuᵢ for conservative loads, U strain energy in terms of displacements
formulas.use: Among admissible displacement fields, equilibrium makes Π stationary and a stable one minimizes it.

formulas.name: Rayleigh-Ritz
formulas.eq: w = Σ aᵢ φᵢ(x),   ∂Π/∂aᵢ = 0  ⟹  K a = f
formulas.where: φᵢ kinematically admissible trial functions satisfying the essential boundary conditions
formulas.use: Gives an approximate solution that is stiffer than exact, an upper bound on stiffness.

formulas.name: Maxwell-Betti reciprocity
formulas.eq: P₁ δ₁₂ = P₂ δ₂₁,   fᵢⱼ = fⱼᵢ
formulas.where: δᵢⱼ displacement at i due to load at j, fᵢⱼ flexibility coefficients, linear elastic
formulas.use: Flexibility and stiffness matrices are symmetric.

formulas.name: Energy stability criterion
formulas.where: Π total potential, qᵢ generalized coordinates, conservative loading
formulas.use: Stability is lost when the Hessian of Π stops being positive definite.

formulas.name: Rigid bar with rotational spring
formulas.eq: Π = ½Cθ² − PL(1 − cos θ),   P_cr = C/L
formulas.where: C rotational spring stiffness at the base, L bar length, P axial load at the tip
formulas.use: Classic stable symmetric bifurcation; the post-buckling path rises as P/P_cr = θ/sin θ.

formulas.name: Rigid bar with lateral spring
formulas.eq: Π = ½k(L sin θ)² − PL(1 − cos θ),   P_cr = kL
formulas.where: k translational spring at the top of a pinned rigid bar of length L
formulas.use: Equilibrium path P = kL cos θ falls after buckling, the canonical unstable symmetric bifurcation.

formulas.name: Multi-DOF linear eigenproblem
formulas.where: K elastic stiffness, K_G geometric stiffness per unit load, φ buckling mode
formulas.use: The lowest eigenvalue gives the critical load and its eigenvector the buckled shape.

formulas.name: Koiter post-buckling expansion
formulas.where: ξ buckling mode amplitude; a ≠ 0 asymmetric, a = 0 with b > 0 stable symmetric, b < 0 unstable symmetric
formulas.use: Initial post-buckling slope and curvature classify the bifurcation and its imperfection sensitivity.

formulas.name: Imperfection sensitivity laws
formulas.where: P_s limit load of the imperfect structure, ε imperfection amplitude
formulas.use: Koiter laws: small imperfections cause large capacity loss in unstable systems.

formulas.name: Degree of indeterminacy
formulas.eq: Planar truss: m + r − 2j;   planar rigid frame: 3m + r − 3j
formulas.where: m members, r reaction components, j joints; zero means determinate if stable
formulas.use: Counts the redundants for the force method.

formulas.name: Force method compatibility
formulas.where: δ₁₀ displacement at the released redundant under real loads, f₁₁ displacement there per unit X₁
formulas.use: Restores compatibility at the release to solve for the redundant force.

formulas.name: Springs in series and parallel
formulas.eq: Series: 1/k = Σ 1/kᵢ;   parallel: k = Σ kᵢ
formulas.where: Series share force, parallel share displacement
formulas.use: Reduces combined elastic supports to one equivalent stiffness.

formulas.name: Member stiffnesses
formulas.eq: Axial EA/L,   cantilever tip 3EI/L³,   torsion GJ/L,   fixed-fixed midspan 192EI/L³
formulas.where: Force per displacement (or torque per rotation) for uniform members
formulas.use: Model structural members as springs in an indeterminate system.

formulas.name: Bar element stiffness
formulas.where: Local axial element, K assembled from all elements, u nodal displacements
formulas.use: Displacement (stiffness) method for statically indeterminate structures.

formulas.name: Classic indeterminate results
formulas.eq: Propped cantilever, uniform w: R = 3wL/8.   Fixed-fixed, uniform w: M_end = wL²/12
formulas.where: R prop reaction, M_end fixed-end moment magnitude, midspan moment wL²/24 for fixed-fixed
formulas.use: Benchmarks for checking force method and slope-deflection answers.

formulas.name: Curved beam bending energy
formulas.where: Thin curved beam, R ≫ depth, ds = R dθ; quarter ring fixed at one end with a radial load P at the free end gives δ = πPR³/(4EI) along P
formulas.use: Castigliano on rings and arches; least work ∂U/∂M₀ = 0 for closed rings.

formulas.name: Winkler curved beam stress
formulas.eq: |σ(r)| = |M| |r − r_n|/(A e r),   r_n = A/∫(dA/r),   e = r̄ − r_n
formulas.where: r radius from the center of curvature, r̄ centroid radius, r_n neutral axis radius
formulas.use: Hyperbolic stress with the neutral axis shifted toward the center and peak stress at the inner fiber.

formulas.name: Transformed section
formulas.eq: n = E₂/E₁,   b₂,eq = n b₂,   σ₂ = n σ_transformed
formulas.where: Material 2 widths scaled by n to equivalent material 1
formulas.use: Turns a multi-material beam into one homogeneous section for the flexure formula.

formulas.name: Modulus-weighted bending
formulas.where: dᵢ distance from each part's centroid to the modulus-weighted neutral axis
formulas.use: Neutral axis moves toward the stiffer material, and stress magnitude is Eᵢ|y||M|/(EI)_eff.

formulas.name: Parallel axial members
formulas.where: Members bonded or rigidly connected so they share one strain
formulas.use: Load splits in proportion to each material's axial stiffness EA.

formulas.name: Sandwich bending stiffness
formulas.where: E_f face modulus, t face thickness, d distance between face centroids, core and face self-bending neglected
formulas.use: Thin faces carry bending as a couple while the core carries shear, giving high stiffness per weight.

formulas.name: Hyperelastic stresses
formulas.where: W strain energy per reference volume, S second Piola-Kirchhoff, P first Piola-Kirchhoff
formulas.use: All stress measures follow from one energy function.

formulas.name: Stress measure conversions
formulas.eq: σ = J⁻¹ P Fᵀ = J⁻¹ F S Fᵀ,   P = J σ F⁻ᵀ
formulas.where: σ Cauchy stress, J = det F; from Nanson's formula n da = J F⁻ᵀN dA
formulas.use: Pushes referential stresses to the current configuration and back.

formulas.name: Invariants of C
formulas.eq: I₁ = tr C,   I₂ = ½[(tr C)² − tr(C²)],   I₃ = det C = J²
formulas.where: In principal stretches: I₁ = Σλᵢ², I₂ = λ₁²λ₂² + λ₂²λ₃² + λ₃²λ₁²
formulas.use: Isotropic hyperelastic energies depend on F only through these invariants.

formulas.name: Incompressible neo-Hookean
formulas.where: μ small-strain shear modulus, p pressure Lagrange multiplier set by boundary conditions
formulas.use: Simplest rubber model, reducing to linear elasticity with ν = ½ at small strain.

formulas.name: Mooney-Rivlin
formulas.where: C₁, C₂ material constants, incompressible
formulas.use: Adds the second invariant to fit rubber data better at moderate stretch.

formulas.name: Neo-Hookean uniaxial tension
formulas.where: λ axial stretch, lateral stretches λ^(−1/2), traction-free lateral faces give p = μ/λ
formulas.use: Large-stretch uniaxial response, with initial slope 3μ = E.

formulas.name: Material time derivative
formulas.where: φ field in spatial description, v velocity, ∂/∂t at fixed x
formulas.use: Rate following a particle: local rate plus convective rate.

formulas.name: Velocity gradient
formulas.eq: L = grad v = Ḟ F⁻¹ = D + W,   J̇ = J div v
formulas.where: D = sym L rate of deformation, W = skew L spin
formulas.use: D measures stretching rate; div v = tr D is the volumetric rate.

formulas.name: Conservation of mass
formulas.eq: ∂ρ/∂t + div(ρv) = 0  ⟺  Dρ/Dt + ρ div v = 0,   ρJ = ρ₀
formulas.where: ρ current density, ρ₀ reference density
formulas.use: Spatial and referential statements of mass balance; isochoric motion has div v = 0.

formulas.name: Reynolds transport theorem
formulas.eq: d/dt ∫_Ω φ dv = ∫_Ω (Dφ/Dt + φ div v) dv
formulas.where: Ω material volume moving with the body; equals ∫ ∂φ/∂t dv + ∮ φ v·n da
formulas.use: Moves time derivatives inside integrals to localize the integral balance laws.

formulas.name: Linear momentum balance
formulas.eq: div σ + b = ρ v̇ (spatial),   Div P + b₀ = ρ₀ v̇ (referential)
formulas.where: b body force per current volume, b₀ = J b per reference volume, Div with respect to X
formulas.use: Cauchy's equation of motion, reducing to equilibrium when acceleration is zero.

formulas.name: Energy balance (first law)
formulas.eq: ρ ė = σ:D − div q + ρ r
formulas.where: e internal energy per mass, q heat flux, r heat source per mass, σ:D stress power
formulas.use: Local energy balance; σ:D = J⁻¹ S:Ė = J⁻¹ P:Ḟ.

formulas.name: Euler buckling load
formulas.where: K effective length factor: 1 pinned-pinned, 2 cantilever, 0.7 fixed-pinned, 0.5 fixed-fixed; r = √(I/A)
formulas.use: Elastic critical load of an ideal straight column.

formulas.name: Beam-column equation
formulas.eq: EI w⁗ + P w″ = 0,   k² = P/(EI)
formulas.where: Uniform column under compressive P, small deflection; general solution w = A sin kx + B cos kx + Cx + D
formulas.use: Applying the boundary conditions gives the buckling eigenvalue problem.

formulas.name: Imperfection amplification
formulas.where: Pinned column with initial sinusoidal imperfection of amplitude δ₀
formulas.use: Deflection grows without bound as P approaches P_cr; the amplification factor is 1/(1 − P/P_cr).

formulas.name: Southwell plot
formulas.where: δ added deflection measured in test, δ₀ initial imperfection
formulas.use: Plotting δ/P against δ gives slope 1/P_cr, so tests yield P_cr and δ₀.

formulas.name: Secant formula
formulas.where: Pinned column, load eccentricity e, c distance to the extreme fiber, r radius of gyration
formulas.use: Peak stress for an eccentrically loaded column, used for yield-based design.

formulas.name: Johnson parabola
formulas.where: Applies for KL/r below the transition slenderness √(2π²E/σ_y)
formulas.use: Inelastic buckling for intermediate columns, tangent to the Euler curve at σ_y/2.

formulas.name: Thermoelastic Hooke's law
formulas.eq: ε = ((1 + ν)/E)σ − (ν/E)(tr σ)I + αΔT I,   σ = λ(tr ε)I + 2με − 3KαΔT I
formulas.where: α coefficient of thermal expansion, ΔT temperature change, K bulk modulus, isotropic
formulas.use: Total strain equals mechanical strain plus free thermal dilatation.

formulas.name: Restrained thermal stress
formulas.eq: Bar: σ = −EαΔT;   plate restrained in plane: σ = −EαΔT/(1 − ν)
formulas.where: Full restraint of the in-plane strain, free out-of-plane surface (σ₃₃ = 0)
formulas.use: Heating a constrained member produces compression with no strain.

formulas.name: Rule of mixtures
formulas.eq: E₁ = V_fE_f + V_mE_m (equal strain),   1/E₂ = V_f/E_f + V_m/E_m (equal stress)
formulas.where: V_f, V_m fiber and matrix volume fractions; Voigt upper and Reuss lower bounds
formulas.use: Fibers govern longitudinal stiffness and the matrix governs transverse stiffness.

formulas.name: Orthotropic reciprocity
formulas.where: ν₁₂ contraction in 2 per extension in 1; follows from a symmetric compliance matrix
formulas.use: Fixes ν₂₁ from the other three in-plane constants of a lamina.

formulas.name: Reduced stiffness of a ply
formulas.eq: Q₁₁ = E₁/(1 − ν₁₂ν₂₁),  Q₂₂ = E₂/(1 − ν₁₂ν₂₁),  Q₁₂ = ν₁₂E₂/(1 − ν₁₂ν₂₁),  Q₆₆ = G₁₂
formulas.where: Plane stress in principal material axes; Q̄ obtained by rotating to the laminate axes
formulas.use: Ply stiffness input to classical lamination theory.

formulas.name: ABD laminate relation
formulas.eq: [N; M] = [[A, B],[B, D]] [ε⁰; κ],   (A, B, D)ᵢⱼ = ∫ Q̄ᵢⱼ (1, z, z²) dz
formulas.where: N, M force and moment resultants per width, ε⁰ midplane strains, κ curvatures, z from midplane
formulas.use: B = 0 for symmetric layups, so extension and bending decouple.
